evidence: The Si substrates employed in this study were cut from p-type (100) Si wafers (LG Siltron) with resistivity in the range of 1–5 V cm. The Si substrates were initially treated with a chemical cleaning process that involved degreasing, HNO3 boiling, NH4OH boiling (alkali treatment), HCl boiling (acid treatment), rinsing in deionized water, and blow-drying with nitrogen to remove contaminants and to grow a thin protective oxide layer on the surface. The fluorinated tin oxide (FTO) glass substrates with a sheet resistance of 10 V/& (Sigma Aldrich) were cut into 1.5 /C2 1.5 cm2 and cleaned with acetone, ethanol, de-ionized water, and blow-dried with nitrogen to remove contaminants, followed by annealing for 10 min at 450 /C14C.
